title: Top of book from L2 updates
statement: Apply level-2 updates [side, price, qty] to an order book (side 0 = bid, 1 = ask; the new qty replaces the level's size; qty 0 removes the level). After every update, output [best_bid, bid_qty, best_ask, ask_qty], using −1 for both numbers of an empty side. Prices are integer ticks.
hints: A map price → size per side; the best bid is the max key, the best ask the min key.
Python has no sorted map: a heap of prices with lazy removal (skip prices no longer in the map).

solution.explanation: A feed handler's core loop. C++: std::map<int,int, greater<>> for bids and std::map<int,int> for asks, with best = begin(). Python: dict + heap with lazy deletion (Part 5's trick). Production versions use arrays indexed by tick offset (Part 10.4) because price bands are narrow. Note the semantics: L2 updates carry the new total size of a level, not a delta, and a missed update corrupts the book, which is why feeds carry sequence numbers.
